subject: fishback

brief.inclusion: Investment manager, debate-organization founder and unsuccessful 2026 Republican candidate for governor of Florida who built a national following around restricting legal immigration, opposing U.S. support for Israel and challenging the Republican Party's donor establishment.
brief.namesakes: James T. Fishback, the Florida investor and 2026 gubernatorial candidate; distinguish him from other people with the surname by Azoria Partners, Incubate Debate and Florida candidate account 89600.

coverage.lags: Florida campaign-finance records are not imported into Worldview's federal FEC tables. Post-primary activity is checked through the October 17 CNN report on his national tour.

openQuestions: Exact birth date is not established by a primary source; reporting described him as 30 in November 2025 and 31 during 2026.
Georgetown and conference biographies say he studied international economics but do not establish that he received a degree.
The date and terms of his departure from Azoria are not established by a company statement; the two Azoria ETFs were liquidated in December 2025.
Refresh Florida campaign receipts and expenditures when the Division of Elections posts final amended reports for the 2026 cycle.
The September 2026 federal lawsuit arising from his removal from the Miami-Dade commission meeting remains unresolved.

summary: James Fishback founded the high-school program Incubate Debate and the investment firm Azoria before running for governor of Florida as a Republican in 2026. He finished third in the primary with about 10.5% of the vote after campaigning against both unauthorized and legal immigration, Florida investment in Israel Bonds, AIPAC influence and establishment Republican donors. After the primary he continued those themes through public meetings and a national speaking tour, presenting his campaign as the start of a broader America First movement.

If you want to go hire thousands of H-1Bs across our state, do whatever you want, but you're not going to get a penny of taxpayer funding.
The immigration moratorium that I support at the federal level and will push for at the state level by using powerful economic deterrence is that, at this point, we are full.

That's why I'm the only candidate in my race who has said I will refuse any dollar from AIPAC.

chapters.title: Debate and political formation
chapters.dek: A Florida debate organizer who made open argument his first public cause.
chapters.body:
Fishback studied international economics at Georgetown University's Walsh School of Foreign Service, according to a later institutional biography; the source does not establish his attendance dates or whether he received a degree [[greenwich-bio-2026]]. In 2019 he founded Incubate Debate, a Florida program that partnered with school districts to run middle- and high-school competitions outside the national debate circuit [[nbc-incubate-2025, campaign-press-2026]].

He later described the project as an answer to ideological restrictions in school debate, and his gubernatorial platform made free speech a recurring theme. That platform combined speech protections with a broader argument for state power against institutions he said disadvantaged Floridians [[campaign-platform-2026]].

chapters.title: Incubate Debate and disputed allegations
chapters.dek: A school-district rupture became part of the record he carried into politics.
chapters.body:
In September 2022 a parent told several Florida school districts that Fishback had begun an inappropriate relationship with a 17-year-old Incubate Debate employee. Broward County said it ended his volunteer work after receiving the allegation. Fishback has denied wrongdoing; he said the allegations were false, that he had never been arrested, charged or convicted, and that a state child-welfare inquiry found no evidence of misconduct [[nbc-incubate-2025]].

The former employee later sought a protective order over alleged harassment after their breakup. The judge denied the petition, finding that Fishback had not harassed her; the ruling did not decide whether the relationship began while she was a minor. NBC also reported that an Incubate adviser resigned after saying Fishback had failed to disclose the allegations to the board. The allegation remains disputed and no criminal charge or adjudication established it [[nbc-incubate-2025]].

chapters.title: Greenlight and Azoria
chapters.dek: A hedge-fund job, a contested departure and two short-lived ETFs.
chapters.body:
Greenlight Capital hired Fishback as a research analyst in 2021. Court records say he began preparing Azoria while still employed, registered its domain in July 2023 and told outside contacts in August that he had resigned and would start the fund [[greenlight-order-2026]]. Greenlight later sued over his use of confidential information and his employment obligations. In a September 2025 settlement Fishback acknowledged sending portfolio and strategy material to a personal account, maintaining an undisclosed trading account and sharing confidential information; he agreed to return or delete the material and pay Greenlight's costs [[greenlight-settlement-2025, greenlight-order-2026]].

Azoria promoted an investment strategy excluding large companies with quantitative demographic hiring targets and introduced it at Mar-a-Lago in December 2024 [[reuters-azoria-2024]]. The Azoria 500 Meritocracy ETF began trading in July 2025, with SEC filings naming Fishback as founder, chief executive and portfolio manager [[sec-azoria-2025]]. It and the Azoria TSLA Convexity ETF stopped trading December 8 and liquidated December 15 after the trust board voted to terminate them [[sec-liquidation-2026]].

chapters.title: The 2026 campaign
chapters.dek: An insurgent candidacy built around immigration, affordability and opposition to Israel-linked power.
chapters.body:
Fishback entered the Republican gubernatorial primary on November 24, 2025, challenging Trump-endorsed Representative Byron Donalds. He paired proposals to eliminate homestead property taxes and subsidize first-home purchases with attacks on both unauthorized immigration and the H-1B program [[ap-launch-2025, campaign-platform-2026]]. Before the primary, Florida Phoenix reported about $705,000 raised by his campaign and more than $1.2 million by the associated Florida First committee; those state transactions are outside Worldview's federal FEC dataset [[florida-phoenix-money-2026]].

In a January interview he said even legal migration could violate the government's social contract, proposed denying state contracts to employers using H-1B workers and supported a broader immigration moratorium. He also promised to refuse AIPAC money, divest Florida public money from Israel Bonds, repeal restrictions on state contractors that boycott Israel and protect criticism of foreign governments as speech [[tac-interview-2026]]. His campaign platform extended the same preference for state intervention to housing, abortion, schools, surveillance and data centers [[campaign-platform-2026]].

chapters.title: Defeat and a national tour
chapters.dek: A third-place finish became the premise for a continuing movement campaign.
chapters.body:
Fishback finished third in the August 18 Republican primary with about 10.5% of the vote; Byron Donalds won the nomination [[florida-candidates-2026, florida-primary-results-2026, cnn-tour-2026]]. The campaign homepage changed its message to: "The race might be over, but our fight is just getting started" [[campaign-home-2026]].

On September 1 he was removed from a Miami-Dade County Commission meeting while trying to oppose a change raising the permitted share of county investments in Israel Bonds from 3% to 5%. Reports said the chair ruled him out of order and that he had not registered to address the item; Fishback later sued the chair, claiming his speech rights were violated [[florida-politics-bonds-2026, jta-bonds-2026]].

By October CNN reported that he had taken the campaign on a national tour. Hundreds attended a Dallas event at which he attacked U.S. involvement in the Iran war and called for the country to "break free from Israel." He told CNN that the primary loss had not changed his approach and framed the tour as a challenge to both major parties and the Republican donor establishment [[cnn-tour-2026]].

chapters.title: America First as economic and foreign-policy separation
chapters.dek: A politics of national preference applied to labor, capital, speech and alliances.
chapters.body:
Fishback's immigration position goes beyond enforcement against unauthorized entry. He has argued for an immigration moratorium and for state economic penalties against employers using H-1B labor, describing legal migration as potentially contrary to a social contract with citizens [[tac-interview-2026, campaign-platform-2026]].

His foreign-policy argument uses a parallel rule: public money and legal privilege should not favor a foreign government. He linked that position to rejecting AIPAC support, divesting public holdings of Israel Bonds and repealing Florida's anti-boycott restrictions. He has also said his views changed as he followed the war in Gaza, describing his earlier failure to attend to Palestinian suffering as a blind spot [[tac-interview-2026]]. After the primary he intensified that argument, presenting opposition to U.S. support for Israel and the Iran war as a dividing line for a younger America First movement inside the Republican Party [[cnn-tour-2026]].
